Question: They say that CMYK is better and more accurate in prints rather than RGB, and I get why. But for some reason, the print I made looks better in RGB. Why is that?
Answer: If you are printing to a CMYK printer, then it’s printing CMYK no matter what setting you use. Physically the printer only has the CMYK toners/inks available to print with. What’s really going on when you print is you are sending information from your computer to the printer. While the information you are sending is speaking RGB, the printer translates that and converts to CMYK so it can print it. This translation happens anytime you send information from your computer to the printer. There are various CMYK color profiles that are translated differently by the printer as there are various RGB color profiles. The profile you pick matters because one profile translates “Blue” differently than another profile. I’ve had artwork saved as RGB print better using a RGB profile instead of using a CMYK profile. Letting the printer translate the artwork from RGB to CMYK itself worked out better than converting to CMYK on my computer. The printer knew the best way to translate the color information.

Question: How can color, line, value, space and shape be used in printing?
Answer: That’s a really interesting question. Color, line, value, space, shape (and texture) are the Elements of Art; something you’d learn in an Art 101 class. You are not trying to get me to do your homework are you? Just kidding. The elements of art are used in printing when anything is printed. The elements are what the designers use to create the artwork that is used for the impression that is printed on whatever material you are using. Paper, vinyl, metal, etc. Whenever you see an advertisement in the mail, buy a product that comes in a box or comes with a manual, or drive past a billboard; you are witnessing the elements of design used to create the graphics that are printed. I noticed that you left out texture in the question. I would incorporate that into the question because there is defiantly texture involved in printing. Beyond the texture of the various papers, metals, vinyls and other materials you can print on, you can print on a material and then have texture incorporated in the process with thermal dye’s, foil stamping, embossing, debossing, etc. Not to mention product packaging which is a 3d object. I can totally understand the omission. I’m sure flat printing was what was being thought of. In conclusion, the elements of art are used in designs and materials that are used in printing. When planning a project they come up in almost every step of the process.

Question: How should one deal with this at a restaurant, ordering a steak dinner with baked potato and actually being served instant potatoes instead, and the manager saying they had run out of baked potatoes?

While many restaurants do have a clause on the menu in fine print that states substitutions may be made or something to that effect, that clause really should only be used as a shield from abusive customers. As a food server I would not be happy and I would really expect the manager to comp the meal (give for free) or at the least give a free dessert or something to the customer if they served them a plate of food they changed without asking first. If they did not do that minor bit of an apology I would start looking for another place to work. Since restaurants do not pay much and I had to rely on tips I need to work in a place that lets me earn as much as I can, not tie my hands. How I would deal with it as a customer who was told by the manager they changed something without asking me first would be to politely say that I wished that they would have asked me first and then if I really did not want instant potatoes and ask for something else. If they did not accommodate me I’d still pay for the meal but I’d let them know that I most likely would not return. Honestly even if they just honored my request without apology I’d still probably not come back. Now if the manager apologized and offered me a token like a free dessert I would surely come back. If the food was good I’d tell others as well. Things go wrong and things do run out. Sometimes the kitchen makes a mistake so if my complaint is acknowledged I know it is a well run establishment.

Question: How does a narcissist typically react when one of his intended victims stands up to him?
Answer: When life throws you something unexpected When my wife told me her mom was having a hard time financially and felt like she had no choice but to invite her to live with us I agreed because it seemed the right thing to do. Boy did we not understand what we were getting ourselves into. My mother in-law “Pat” immediately exhibited some very odd behaviors. Things that seemed reasonable to us set Pat off on long rants. Any sort of criticism or suggestion of altering any of Pat’s behavior led to conflict. After much research and reading up on ways to cope and bring peace in my home, I have to conclude Pat is suffering from some sort of disorder and while I have no credentials to give a diagnosis, I can only conclude she suffers from a form of NPD (Narcissitc Personality Disorder). Here is a sampling of how she would react when confronting or standing up to behaviors that made my wife and I uncomfortable. Pat’s and how she always makes it about her: Pat always interrupts when you are talking. It does not matter what you are doing, Pat will start speaking from the other side of the house and walk into the room like nothing else is going on. If you try to correct her by saying “Excuse me but we were in the middle of speaking” or “Give me a second” Pat will become indignant and exclaim “Boy, I just can’t say anything” or “Oh I’m not allowed to speak, sorry” Another incident I recall is one day my wife started getting calls from family members asking her if she was alright. My wife was very confused by this and was told her mom told them my wife had a medical procedure and was recovering from it. What my wife had done was a simple outpatient procedure done that had to do with her lady parts. My wife was very embarrassed and asked her mom why she’d do this. With great indignation her mom responds: “What would you have me do? You did have a procedure done. Did you want me to lie?” and then followed up with an exasperated “Fine I won’t mention you again. I won’t say anything. I’m always the bad guy.” My in-law Pat sleeps all day and is up all night. This means while my wife and I are trying to get a decent night sleep so we can work the next day, Pat is up all night washing dishes, organizing the refrigerator and pantry we bought her (we had to do this cause sharing space with Pat is exhausting so she needed her own fridge), and doing all sorts of chores which makes my dogs bark all night waking us up. It makes my neighbors dogs bark too cause she throws out the trash and cleans her car after midnight (our neighbors are less than thrilled with this.) This makes our motion sensor lights go on all night and we can’t find curtains thick enough to fully block the light. You can ask, you can beg but anything you say about it will lead to her saying she’s picked on, she’s not allowed to do anything, she’s a prisoner, etc. For Thanksgiving we always drive to my wife’s brothers home in another state. This is a very long drive, especially because Pat can’t go 50 miles without going to a rest stop, which takes at least 15 min each stop so a 6 hour drive turns to 9. Due to Pat’s lifestyle of sleeping all day and being awake all night it is very difficult to get her to leave at a decent hour that lets me drive while I’m still awake enough to be safe. No matter how well we plan she always delays and delays until you are forced to practically drag her from the home to get into the car. She deftly parries any attempts to get her to move along into us being mean and picking on her. My wife is trying hard to lose weight. After telling her mom that she’s not eating breads and pastas in an effort to reduce carbohydrates, her mom starting buying loafs of bread for us. In her mom’s mind “It’s ok to eat a little bit.” and she’s just trying to be nice. Repeated requests to please not buy us bread or cake falls on deaf ears and leads to more of my in-law saying how she can’t do anything nice and never gets credit for anything. As a bonus we get to hear how broke Pat is even though she finds the money to buy us things we neither want nor need. Question: If cyan, magenta, and yellow already make black, then why is black another component of the CMYK model? And why doesn’t RGB have white as a color component when red, green, and blue make white?
Answer: Black is very necessary for quality color printing. The reason is the inks used in offset printing are translucent. They are not opaque or solid and the paper color can and will show though the colors printed. This will effect the final result and the color as seen. Try printing 100% Cyan on a sheet of uncoated paper with two different brightness ratings and you will see the shade of Cyan will differ slightly on each sheet of paper. The colors also show though each other when they overlap. If you print 100% of CMY on top of each other you will have a dark muddy brown color, not the black that color theory says it should. There is also a physical limit of how much wet ink you can place on a sheet of paper before the paper is soaked though and the ink starts to spread. This is not a good thing when it happens. The limit is roughly 300%. You do not want the total percentage of ink you drop on a sheet of paper to ever exceed 300% so trying to get 100% of CMY to make a black is already putting you at the edge of the limit. Not good. So black is added in to add contrast and tone. As to the second part of your question, RGB does not need to add white because light is light. There are no physical properties such as a paper’s color to interfere with the RGB colors so when you combine RGB together you will get a pure white color. It all comes down to the physical properties of light (RGB) vs pigment (CMYK) http://learn.leighcotnoir.com/artspeak/elements-color/primary-colors/#:~:text=

Question: How do I set up a trifold brochure in InDesign?
Answer: A tri-fold brochure is simply a sheet of paper folded into 3 panels. The most common tri-fold in the USA used a letter-sized sheet (8.5″x11″) folded into 3 panels. So make a document that is 11″x8.5″ (landscape) design your brochure. The most common mistake in designing brochures I’ve seen is that people tend to divide the sheet into 3 equal panels. This seems reasonable but falsely assumes the finished product will have equal panels once printed and folded. We (printers) have to trim the panel that gets folded inside a little shorter to ensure a smooth fold. If you just fold the paper evenly the inside panel will buckle. I advise making the inside panel 1/16th of an inch smaller when you design to keep an even look to the art and ensure it brochure folds smoothly. An easy way to do this is to set up a guide for each panel. A sheet of paper has 2 sides and for a brochure we call them the outside and the inside. The outside being the part you see when the brochure is folded. So if you are viewing the outside page when designing and going from left to right. make each of the three panels the following dimensions: 3.6″,3.7″,3.7″. You reverse this on the inside page and going from left to right: 3.7″,3.7″,3.6″ PRO TIP: Make sure you leave at least a 1/8th inch margin on each of the 4 edges on the sheet. Do not put any text or graphic elements inside that margin. This will give a clean and balanced look to your brochure. No printing method can ensure a perfectly squared and centered impression on a every printed sheet of paper. Printing is a mechanical process and things and move around slightly. Cutting & folding can even make things even more uneven. I’m not talking huge differences but our eye can pick up even the smallest variation. If you have a solid shape or some text close than 1/8th of an inch to the edge, then even a small imbalance of 1/32nd on an inch or less really stands out to the eye. Giving a little room between your graphic elements and the edge of the sheet of paper makes a huge difference in perceived quality.

Question: How do I convert an appearance pattern to vector in Illustrator whilst maintaining transparency?
Answer: For simplicity I’m assuming you have a black & white pattern and you want the white part transparent though this will work regardless of the colors as long as you have solid shapes in the raster image you want to convert to vectors. After conversion I’d expect you to have black shapes and white shapes in that graphic, the white shapes will be filled and will not be transparent if you use something like the auto trace feature of Illustrator. There may be a setting to use that I’m not familiar with but what I’d do in this situation is click on a white shape after it is turned to a vector and select all with the same color fill option. That will select all the white parts and you should be able to delete them thus having a “transparent” background. If the black and white shapes and connected and you can’t delete the white without the black going away then here is a hack I discovered. Select all of the same fill as I mentioned above. All of the white shapes will highlight (even though they may be connected to the black) Select “hide” for the white parts you selected. Select “show hidden” the white will come back but this time only the white parts you want to delete will be really selected. Now you can delete at will. As an alternative you could just make the white fill in the shapes transparent but I think best practice would be to remove unneeded shapes in the graphic. Some images are more complex than others so results will vary. For the best chances of converting your pattern from raster to vector you want the sharpest image with the most solid colors and the most contrast between shapes you can start with. I often photoshop the image and blow the contrast to the max. Hope that is clear. If not ask and I’ll try to clarify. Good luck.

Question: How are CMYK and RGB, both primary colours?
Answer: Most of us learn in Kindergarten that the primary colors are red, yellow and blue. You use these three primary colors to mix up almost any other color you want. In art school they advance this further by listing the secondary (Green, Orange and Violet) and tertiary colors (Yellow Orange, Orange Red, Red Violet, Blue Violet, etc.) that result from mixing the primaries. When you mention primary colors anyone outside the printing industry is going to think in these terms. So how are CMYK and RGB primary colors? Well the definition of primary colors is simply a group or set of colors that can be combined to to produce a gamut or range of colors. Commercial printing mostly revolves around 2 sets of colors. CMYK and RGB. CMYK or 4 color process printing combines Cyan, Yellow, Magenta and Black (yes K is Black) to mix up the gamut of colors needed for color printing. Every shade you see on the printed page is made of a mixture of these four primary colors. RGB is a mixture of Red, Green and Blue and they mix in much the same way as CMYK does to create every shade within it's gamut. RGB has a much larger gamut and much richer colors. In each printing system they are both considered the primary colors since you use that specific set to create the colors within it's range. So that's how CMYK and RGB can be primary colors. If you want to understand color theory better here is a link. Color Theory Basics - Additive and Subtractive Color Mixing

Question: What is the most useful piece of unexpected advice you have ever received?
Answer: When I found out that my bank account unexpectedly empty it led me to darkness and depression. Luckily advice from a unlikely source pulled me back and turned things around. My dilemma: It was roughly a year after I packed up my things from Long Island, New York and drove across the nation to Los Angeles, California. I was tending bar and making good money. Life was looking up. It was about a week into the new year when I got a message from my apartment manager saying my rent check bounced. This seemed absurd to me as I had plenty of cash so surely this was a bank mistake. Telling the manager I'd take care of this I phone the bank to see what's going on. Calling the bank I found out only was my account cleaned out I was also overdrawn $800. All the transactions that emptied my account came from a casino that I'd never been to on a night that I was working. I told the bank I wanted to file a fraud claim. What happened over the next month between myself and Bank of America was ridiculous and is a story in of itself. Evil Banks: I eventually was put in touch with the security division of Bank of America. I asked for the ATM photos to see who pulled out the money. BoA refused unless the police department requested it. The police had no idea what I was talking about when I asked them for help getting the photos. They’d never heard of the bank not giving out the ATM photos. The detective I filed a report with gave a perplexed shake of his head and helped me get the photos from the bank. It was not me in the photo. It was someone I’d never seen before. I told the bank I never lost or gave my card to anyone and this as not me. The bank told me it was impossible to forge a debit card so I must have given it to someone to use. This was clearly a lie as just that same month a huge story broke in the news about how the San Francisco police busted a crime ring that was in fact doing that very thing; forging ATM cards. When I told the BoA security person I was talking to about it they hung up on me. My rent check bounced, all my utility and credit card payment checks bounced, everything bounced. It was taking weeks to get anywhere with Bank of America and not only would they not help me, they wanted the $800 back and were charging me fees for all the bounced checks so I had no money, was starting to get in real trouble for bad checks, was about to lose my apartment. Panic was setting in. The advice that saved me: Weeks passed and eventually I exhausted my options with the bank and the police. I made very good money tending bar but it was a difficult hole to climb out of. One day at work I was talking about my woes to one of the waitresses who was being very supportive when suddenly I hear an "excuse me" from behind. I turn and see the guy who's job is to take care of all the plants and flowers around the hotel who was attending to his duties in the bar. He begs my pardon for eavesdropping but say he think he might be able to help me out. To my surprise he worked for the comptroller of currency in San Francisco before turning to the field of floristry (is floristry a word?) He said what he heard from me was so awful and so wrong he felt compelled to jump in. He wrote some federal banking code section numbers down on a cocktail napkin and tells me exactly what to say. He tells me to ask the BoA security guys name and to tell him all these code violations that were BoA’s fault and then tell him that I will be contacting the Comptroller of Currency and the President of Bank of America and I will put his name on the letter unless they give me back all my money right now. Turns out by law at the time you were only liable for $50 max in a bank fraud situation as long as you tell the bank about it within 30 days of getting your statement. Also at the time it was against Bank of America corporate policy (or maybe it was a bank code, I can't remember) to let anyone withdraw more than $300 a day from an ATM. I had thousands stolen. So I call the bank asking for the gentlemen I had been dealing with. It took awhile to reach him since he was ducking my calls but eventually I got him and started rattling off what I was told to say. "According to Section C of the federal banking code… and I went into it. Told it all to him and told him about the letter I'd be writing. After a long pause I the voice on the phone says "Mr Vollono, you will be able to pick up your money at the branch tomorrow." Victory: Victory from defeat! All due to a kind eavesdropper. The strangest part is I never saw the florist again and I worked at the Biltmore for another couple years. If you were a florist in the Biltmore hotel in LA in the mid 90s and gave a young bartender some banking advice and are reading this.. Thanks man. You really saved my ass.

Question: Do I need to convert all the linked RGB images to CMYK, before sending an InDesign document for printing, if the InDesign document itself is CMYK?
Answer: “Should you convert your linked RGB images to CMYK before sending them to the printer?” This is the question that needs to be addressed. The program you use is not important to choosing if you need to convert files from RGB to CMYK. It used to be the standard best practice to do so before digital printing came to be. Since printing was done on a printing press, all images had to be separated into process colors (CMYK) for the plates to be made to print with. If you wanted to get any preview as to how your color would look after this conversion you had to be the one to convert the colors to review them before going to the printer. As you gain experience, you build relationships with printers who know what they are doing. You learn to anticipate how a color is going to look after conversion and you can leave it up to your printer to convert the colors. These days with digital printers you might be better off leaving your files RGB if that is closer to how you want them to look. I used to run a Konica 600 and a Ricoh 650 and I found leaving the RGB to CMYK conversion up to the copiers printed a much better result than converting to in InDesign or whatever to CMYK. This especially held true with files created in Microsoft programs like Word or Publisher. Word can’t create CMYK and most people don’t know how to use Publisher enough to figure it out. The RGB blues used in those programs will turn purple if you convert to CMYK. They stay blue if I leave it to the printer. So in summary, if you know what you are doing, want control and are comfortable knowing the result you will get then convert yourself. If you’re not that sure, leave it to your printer. And get a hard-copy proof if color is any concern to you at all! No proof no complaining about color!

Question: Why do PNG files sometimes have "black" backgrounds even though they are transparent?
Answer: Why do PNG files sometimes have “black” backgrounds even though they are transparent? Your question needs more context. What are you trying to accomplish that the black backgrounds are appearing? I’m going to assume you mean printing. This is by far the most common action where I can get odd backgrounds and other printing errors involving a transparent background Depending on what program you are using and what print settings you are using, transparent objects do not always play nice and you can get boxes, missing pieces, strange colors and background shades appearing around your transparent object. The majority of the time I find it is a spot color that is causing the issue. Spot colors and transparency do not play nice with each other. No matter the cause, the best method of fixing it is flattening transparency. Each program does it in a different way so you need to see if you have any options to flatten the transparency. Flattening transparency will take all the objects on your page and flatten them into one single image thus eliminating your software from having to interpret what is going on. There’s a more technical way to describe it but I’m going for simplicity in my explanation. You might ask why we don’t just flatten everything to avoid problems in the first place. There is a good reason. Flattening transparency can cause problems as well. You have to pay careful attention to your fonts, images and any special effects such as drop shadows in case something changes in them when you flatten transparency. Also your flattened file will also be much, much larger than your original. Basically it turns your artwork into one large image. This could cause a printer to crash if you don’t have the processing power to print very large file sizes. If you are going to a commercial printer it will take them a lot longer to process and print a large file so this might be a consideration too if you are in a super rush. Without knowing more about your specific situation this is the best guess I can offer as to what is causing problems.

Question: How do I make screenshots look good when printed in CMYK?
Answer: The proper answer is you can’t. Screen shots are RGB images taken at low resolution. The are not acceptable print quality for any respectable print shop. That said, at times I’ve had to make use of screenshots due to the customer having nothing else available so there are ways to make due. 2) Shrink them down when you can. Shrinking the screenshot size down as much as you can increases the amount of resolution you can squeeze out of it. You really don’t want to make the image bigger as this will just increase the flaws in the image. 3) Clean the image up. If you have some kind of photo editor you can clean the image up a little. Use some sharpening tools, airbrush out any flaws, play with the contrast and up the color saturation a bit. There’s no one answer as it varies greatly depending on the image. 4) Photographs reproduce better than text. A screenshot of a photo is much more forgiving than screenshots of text or shapes. This has to do with rasters vs vectors. 5) You asked about CMYK printing but I offer this in case you just didn’t know to consider it. Print on a digital printer. A digital printer with the right capabilities can print out RGB images much better than a printing press. Many of them have RGB conversion profiles that do a really good job of keeping the RGB color intact. Good luck

Question: What dish names have you seen that you thought were something else, such as "chicken-fried steak" that some people think is chicken?

Question: As a restaurant worker, do you find it suspicious when a diner finds something odd in their food? How do you normally react?

I don’t get odd feelings about people often but this time this couple was just not reading square to me. They ordered several appetizers, wine, salads and entrées. They ate heartily. I told the manager what I saw and he went over to the table with me to talk to the two customers for a few minutes. At this point I’d love to say they were tossed out on their asses but the manager decided it was not worth the trouble to start a conflict and just told them to never mind the bill and to have a good night. The couple left without further trouble. This taught me a lesson. If customers found something odd in their meal, I would just apologize and offer them their food for free. Question: What's the weirdest thing you've ever seen happen in a restaurant?
Answer: As a waiter I’ve encountered many degrees of strange in the restaurants I’ve worked at but one night this customer in particular took the prize for bizarre. It wasn’t a very busy night. A group of four got seated at my table, a young couple and an older couple. I approached them, introduced myself and recited the evening’s specials which included a fish entree, the exact fish is gone from my memory since this was a couple of decades ago. I started taking everyone’s order when the older gentleman said “This fish sounded good I’ll have that.” I got everyone’s order down and went into the kitchen to place their order. Not too long after their food was ready and I set it onto a tray and brought it out to their table. When I put the plate of fish down in front of the gentleman, his face wrinkled up in confusion and disgust. He exclaims “What the hell is this?” Puzzled myself I answered “The fish special you ordered, is something wrong?” He nods “Yes something is wrong, I hate fish. Where’s my steak?” Now I’m starting to perspire. Did I mistake what he said? My mind was rewinding and going over the order. I clearly remembered him asking for the fish special. There was no steak special that night and if he asked for steak I would have asked how he wanted it done. No. I was certain I heard him right. I started looking around the table for support and noticed puzzled looks and whispering among his companions. “I’m sorry, I’m not sure what to say. I thought you asked for the fish but.. I can take this back and get you a steak if you prefer no problem.” He pushes the plate away. “No forget it, I’ve lost my appetite.” His son leans over to my aid “Dad, come on, you did ask for the fish we all heard you.” The older gentlemen shakes his head “No, no I didn’t, I hate fish I’d never order it.” One of the ladies looks at me mouthing “I”m so sorry.” At this point I’m assuming the gentlemen is suffering from some sort of disorder. I just tried to roll with it “Sir, it is really no problem, I’d be happy to get you a steak or whatever you want.” He just declines with a wave of his hand. So I just apologized again and said I’d be sure to take this off the bill. I took the plate away and went into the kitchen with a story to share. The group ate rather quickly and left me a very nice tip. I think they ended up leaving me the cost of the fish special and a tip on the check if my memory is correct.

Question: During your time in the military, did you ever see something that made you say, “you can’t be serious…”?
Answer: In my short stint in the US Air force (you can see why it was short here Francis Vollono's answer to What are you banned from? Why?) I’ve seen a few things that made me say “You can’t be serious” The dormitory I lived in was a three story building that had rooms that two airmen would share and a few common areas like showers and the recreation room we’d all share. Each resident would rotate a few days of janitorial duty to maintain the common areas. One time during my stint on clean up duty I got into a situation that would lead to future troubles, but that’s for another answer. I spent my work day doing what I was instructed to do. Clean the bathrooms, vacuum the carpets, empty out the trash and ashtrays in the common areas (yes we all could smoke inside in those days - oh the 80’s.) Keep in mind that not everyone worked the same hours. So we had dozens of airmen living in the dorms so there were people coming and going at all times. This particular afternoon our First Sergeant comes in for an inspection. I was on the upper floor when someone ran up the stairs to get me because the First Sergeant asked for the guys on clean up duty and he wasn’t happy. I ran down and assembled with the other airmen on clean up duty and listened a 10 minute dressing down by the First Sergeant. “Look at this crap, there’s ashes in the ashtrays” he says walking through the rec room. He walks to the bathroom and wipes a finger in the sink. ‘This is unacceptable, there’s water beads in these sinks, you need to wipe them down.” he continues on with a few other infractions that are troubling him. Now here comes the “You can’t be serious moment” Me: “Sir, well I already ran though the bathrooms and cleaned up the sinks and we already emptied out the ashtrays. People are in the shower right now and people are washing up, the sink is going to get wet. Should we close the bathrooms during the day? I don’t understand.” I didn’t stop there. “Also people are smoking right now, how can we keep ashes out of the ashtrays? What are the ashtrays for exactly?” If I could just go back in time and unsay these things. I should have known better but I was 17 and could not control myself at that time. The First Sergeant just wanted to flex his power on us. A “Yes sir, we’ll do better’ would have just made him leave quickly and we could have all gone on our way and he would have forgotten all about it by the time he to wherever he was going next. Instead I had to be outspoken in my confusion and what it got me was lecture on respect, rank, duty and several other things and the entire dormitory got called out to a meeting where the Sergeant displayed is displeasure at the conditions of the dorm including how disgusting it was that he found fluorescent condoms all over the grass outside the dorm (we had a balloon fight that day) It was a good life lesson. Just because you are right, you don’t always need to let everyone know you are right. At the end of the day was it really a big deal to get a short lecture on cleanliness, even if it was wrong? The universe would have carried on just fine if I kept quiet and perhaps this would not have snowballed into bigger issues for me with my First Sergeant.

Question: What are delicious easy recipes to try cooking when you are just learning how to cook?
Answer: Cooking meat in a pan is something that I often see people not quite get right and it’s very easy to do and delicious. The general principal is to heat up an iron skillet on the stove, very hot. Heat some butter or oil in the skillet and add your meat. You want to cook the meat a few minutes on each side to give it a nice browned appearance. This is called searing. You aim is not to fully cook the meat. You are going to take that skillet and put it inside a pre-heated oven. I like to use 375 degrees but it may vary for you. You can leave the skillet in the oven for 6–12 minutes. It varies with the cut of meat and it’s thickness. 12 minutes is just about right for me when cooking very thick boneless chicken breasts. That’s the basic idea and you get tender, juicy meat every time. To kick it up a notch, I marinate my chicken for 20 minutes or so. For 3 large boneless chicken breasts I put the chicken in a plastic zip lock bag or a bowl I have handy. Pour in about half a cup of lemon juice. a few cloves of garlic that I minced. Enough olive oil to coat the meat, a healthy dose of salt and pepper and some chopped fresh parsley. You can use any herbs you have on hand. If you only have dried herbs you want to only use a few pinches as it’s much stronger tasting than fresh herbs. Cooking meat this way is just a basic technique. You can really do a lot with it using various marinades or sauces. Sky’s the limit!

Question: What recipes or hacks do you have to reduce food waste at home?
Answer: I’m probably a bad person to ask how to reduce food waste because I probably waste a ton of food. I cook more than I can eat and usually have to toss some away because I get lazy about packing and freezing stuff for later. My biggest tip would be to not cook more than you can eat! That said, I do have some ways I do like to use up food that may be getting a bit old or is leftover from other meals instead of throwing it out. Soups: You can toss almost anything in a pot of water and season it enough to make a decent soup. If I have any leftover veggies that are getting a bit too old to eat raw, some leftover cooked meats (Ham and Pork bones are great), I toss them into a pot with some chicken broth or water and bouillon if I don’t have any broth around. You can even toss in a can of beans or some pasta if you want to bulk it up a bit. Toss in a little salt & pepper and maybe a bay leaf and slow cook it for a couple hours and you can have a delicious soup. Fritattas: This is like a quiche but without the pastry crust. It’s just eggs and whatever you have laying around, then you bake it in a skillet in the oven. Your base is eggs, a splash of milk or cream or even butter, then just toss in whatever you have laying around. Meats, cheese, veggies, whatever. Another good leftover clearer. Smoothies: Have some fruit thats too ripe to eat? I hate mushy fruit, there’s nothing unhealthy about it and it’s really sweet and flavorful but I can’t get past the mushy texture. So I toss that ripe fruit in the blender with some yogurt or almond milk or ice, or any other liquid I have around and blend it up into a yummy smoothie. Salads: Have some leftover chicken, turkey or ham? Chop it up into small bits, mix in some celery, onion, carrot, or red peppers minced up small if you have it, add few spoonfuls of mayo and you got your self a meal!. I can eat this in a sandwich, or over some lettuce. Even can just eat it in a bowl with some crackers. It’s a good way to get rid of leftovers without tossing it away. I hope this inspires you to use up some of the food you might be tossing away.

Question: Do you have a recipe that is easy, yet make you look like you really know how to cook?
Answer: Back in the day when dinosaurs roamed the earth, and I was dating, there was one dish I could make for dinner that always scored me huge points and it was so easy to make. Pasta with garlic & oil. Just need a few ingredients. You just need a few ounces of Olive Oil. (Use the best quality extra virgin olive oil you can find/afford as it is the key to the dish.) A few cloves of garlic (or more, more garlic is always good use as much as you can tolerate) Slice the garlic cloves up super-thin, or you can mince it if you lack knife skills. Don’t ever use garlic in a jar, it’s a very sad substitute for fresh garlic. Use the pasta of your choice - I think Spaghetti works best but use what you got. A dash of red pepper flakes. Grated parmesan cheese. **** Bonus points if you can score some fresh basil. It’s available in most markets and only costs a few bucks. Mince up that basil if you got it it will be awesome. Boil your pasta as to the box directions. I always cook it about a minute less than the directions myself. Strain the pasta but do not ever rinse it off! You want that nice starch to stay on it so your sauce sticks to the pasta. **** Bonus if you can reserve a few cups of the pasta water. This can be a nice addition to our dish. Now you can start to cook like a pro! In a skillet heat up your oil and garlic. Get it to a very mild sizzle making sure to stir the garlic often, do not let it brown. Garlic gets bitter if it browns (unless your roasting it of course, then it’s YUM) Add your sprinkle of red pepper flakes to the skillet, after a couple minutes when the garlic starts to look translucent, add in your pasta and toss it well. You want the pasta to be well coated with oil so add more oil if needed. At this point you can pour in a cup of the reserved pasta water. This will make a creamy sauce. Once everything is tossed well and heated through your done. Remove the skillet from the heat, plate your pasta, sprinkle on the basil if you have it and use lots of parmesan cheese. Cheap, easy, tasty. I’ve never gone wrong cooking this dish. It’s probably why my wife married me. Enjoy!

Question: What would you do if your direct superior is flagging every tasks she requests as urgent, despite everybody knows the tasks are not that urgent? We are applying rocket speed to execute every tasks assigned. This has created a stressful environment.
Answer: I experience similar situations at my work. I’ve found I get stress during two conditions. First is if my boss is giving me a task to do when I already have tasks that I feel are more important. It’s stressful when you know you don’t have time for everything. In this case I suggest telling your boss this. “I was going to do Task A just now, but since you want me to do Task B I’ll put that off and work on this.” This lets your boss know what you are doing and gives him the option to decide what the priority is. You might feel Task A is more important and you can make your case as to why it’s more important, but the boss is the boss so pass the buck up to him and let him stress about it. You’ve covered your butt by asking. The Second condition would be that my boss keeps giving me a series of tasks, each one being “urgent” to him. At this point I would tell him exactly what I’m doing. “Hey, I’m trying to do Task A, B and C. You just asked me to do Task D now. There’s no way I can get all this done today so did you want me to drop everything else and finish Task D? What’s your priority for these tasks?” Again this tell him what you are doing and lets him pick the priorities. There is no need for you to stress about it. To me the key is communication. I see so many people just holding it in, complaining to everyone else but the boss they are overworked and can’t get all their work done. I feel it’s my responsibility to keep my boss updated on things and what’s going on. If I don’t say something he’ll just think I have it all under control and pile more work on me. In fact, this has led me to become a most valued and trusted employee for my boss. Just be upfront and as long as you can clearly state what your are doing and why you can’t get it all done you should be ok with any reasonable human being. If after this they are unreasonable then there is nothing you can do that would be right and I would quietly seek another job while doing the best you can.

Question: What is the biggest myth about the production of movies?
Answer: What is the biggest myth about the production of movies? The one I’m aware of is that the job of the Actors is easy or glamorous. In the 1990’s I worked for a film locations company in Los Angeles. This was a company that people filming TV and movies would go to to rent buildings and outdoor areas to film at. I must have observed a few dozen productions filmed in my time and let me tell you I could not be an actor. The film production team can spend hours setting up lights, cameras and props. They then bring out the actor who’s been in a trailer for those hours to give 5 minutes worth of lines. Then the actor goes back to the trailer and they either move things around to redo that same 5 minutes of lines again or move on to another shot. That is so tedious. It was painful for me to watch. Also they sometimes have to say the same 30 second line a dozen or more times. They have to say it the same way, with the same excitement and emotion that they had on the first take. Now some of the really big stars do have awesome trailers with every convenience you can think of but still, your sitting on your ass for hours waiting to say a few sentences. Sometimes the actors have to stand in the same spot for long periods of time also. If it’s a stunt or special effects shoot it is very time consuming and expensive to get all the pieces in place. If something is going wrong or needs to change they can ask the actor to stand still basically till they work it out. Much easier than dissembling the shot to redo later. Sure they get paid a ton, they do have glamorous lifestyles outside of work but I don’t know if I even had the ability if that’s something I’d desire. Kind of like watching sausage be made.

Question: Why do so many people seem to dislike eating fish?

The last time I had really amazing fish was about 15 years ago on a business trip to Hong Kong. I was served a whole fish that came out on a sizzling plate. The waiter poured a sauce of scallions, ginger, sesame oil and soy sauce over the fish. It was incredible. The supermarket fish is all frozen. Granted it might be frozen fresh but to me it’s not the same thing. I’m much older now and I don’t work at this fantastic restaurant anymore. I still don’t really eat fish much cause when I approach the fish counter at the market I smell that fishy smell and my stomach tumbles I suspect this is why people who don’t like fish hate fish. Question: Have you ever walked out of a doctor's office because the doctor was being disrespectful to you?
Answer: Have you ever walked out of a doctor’s office be because the doctor was being disrespectful to you? Absolutely! In my early 20s I developed a sharp pain in my big toe. At first it was making it uncomfortable to walk. I would limp around for a day or two and then it would go away. At times the sharp pain was the most intense thing I’ve ever felt in my life. The pain grew more intense over time and started to last longer. I would take a day off work here and there because of it. It grew to the point I could not wear a shoe or a sock or even tolerate the weight of a sheet on my foot and the pain would last over a week. One day my foot swelled up and and the pain was so bad in my big toe I could barely contain myself from screaming. It was getting red and looked a bit like this I asked my girlfriend (who’s now my wife) to take me to the emergency room. I grabbed a crutch and off we went. After a bit of a wait in the reception area, I was led into a exam room where I waited again. The whole time I was doubled over, wincing, sobbing and crying out in pain. I listened to the doctor outside my room talking and laughing about how her weekend was for a good 15 minutes and finally she walks in. I tell her whats going on and she kinda tilts her head and asks me: “Well, what did you do to it? You drop something on your foot or were you jumping a lot?” I told her “No, I didn’t do anything. This pain comes and goes and has been getting worse over the past year. I’ve tried everything over the counter for pain and nothing helps.” Shaking her head she tells me “Well, people don’t just wake up in pain for no reason, you must have done something.” Again I protest and she writes something down and hands it to me. “This is a prescription for Naproxin.” I knew what Naproxin was. It was basically an over the counter medicine that I told her I tried even at large doses to no effect. I just crumpled the script and tossed in the trash limping out. “Thanks for nothing” I said as I left The pain went away again a few days later. I dealt with it over the next year or so, but I was missing too much work and the attacks were becoming more frequent. I made a regular doctor appointment at the same medical center as the emergency room because I had a HMO and that’s where I had to go. I limp into the appointment and the check in nurse looks at me and my foot and says “Honey, you’ve got Gout.” Gout is basically a build up of uric acid in your bloodstream. It forms crystals like this Notice how they look all sharp and pointy? This is why it hurts like hell. It acts like sandpaper in your blood and builds up in your joints and can be very serious and lead to all kinds of kidney disorders. It’s very rare in someone as young as I was. I talked to the nurse and she looked horrified about my previous visit and asked the doctor’s name. I had the feeling she wanted to get her in trouble, but I had forgotten who she was at that point. The new doctor took good care of me and I got the Gout under control. No more attacks at all anymore, but sadly it did some major damage to my joints. I should have gone back to the doctor sooner than I did, but I always hated going to the doctor and that first visit really left a bad taste in my mouth.

Question: What was your shortest tenure in a job before walking out and why?
Answer: What was your shortest tenure in a job before walking out and why? The shortest I ever lasted in a job was 2 hours. I’m not even sure I lasted even that long. When I moved from New York to Los Angeles in 1992 a friend of mine was a stock broker. He claimed to be having great success with it and was always on me to get into the business. He gave me the phone number of a friend of his who had a brokerage in LA and said I should contact him if I needed work. So I finally get to LA and figure “Why not?” I’ll give this guy a call. I did and he was very friendly and very excited and said sure he could hook me up with a job. I wasn’t sure what to expect but when I arrived to his office it looked something like this. There was a bunch of people, dressed nicely, packed in a room in cubicles on the phone. The place was buzzing and the odor of Drakkar was thick. So I’m told what I’ll be doing is “Cold Calling”. I was given a list of names of people who reported income of $100,000 or more and then I was given another sheet with a “Script” on it. My instructions were to call down the list and read the script to them and get their information in order for the broker to call them back. The script was some story of how good some investment was and how much the guy I was calling for has made people. I don’t recall it exactly. I was going down the list. People mostly replied “No thanks” and hung up. Maybe some were a bit ruder than that. One call I made was to an elderly gentleman. I’m pretty sure part of the “Script” mentioned something about them making over $100,000 because the man I called said “Oh...well yes I made that much but my wife just passed and I had to sell our home and I’m actually broke now” he went on a bit with a very sad tale of misfortune. I felt so bad for even bothering this man. I told him that I was so sorry to hear all that, sorry for bothering you and I hope things do turn around some day. The guy who hired me (I can’t even remember his name) was standing behind me and when I was done with the call he proceeded to lose his shit. Him: “What the fuck! I told you stick to the script.” Me: “I did but then he told me he had no money and I felt bad. I’m not sure what the problem is here.” Him: “You stick to the script and you get their fucking money. That’s what the fuck I’m paying you for. Read the script and move on. Slap ‘n move, slap ‘n move!” He literally is pumping his hands down and gyrating his hips as he is exclaiming this. At this point I look around the room and I see half the room is on the phone distressed and losing money, the other half is cheering like a Roman crowd at a Spartacus match - I guess they were making money. I stood up, held out my hand and said “Thanks for the opportunity but this isn't for me. Have a great day” The guy was taken back totally confused. “What?” is all he could manage.” I just said “Yeah, this isn’t for me at all.” and walked out. I think that was the shortest I ever worked at a job.

Question: What are you banned from? Why?
Answer: I am banned from ever rejoining the US Air Force. Background: I enlisted in the USAF at age 17. Tested really high on the asvab and was able to pick pretty much any job I wanted. I chose to be a Crew Chief. I did well on my training and hoped I would be assigned to this beast of an aircraft: I did get it! I was super excited. After some time, I was excelling in my training and doing well enough that when my supervisor retired (when I was in service, you had a supervisor crew chief and an assistant or two, depending on the aircraft), they left me, the assistant, alone on the aircraft. The supervisors on either side of me on the flight line would look in on me and sign off on things that were above my grade. What went wrong: One day, we received a TO, that’s a tech order, stating something you have to do regarding the aircraft. The TO said to ground all planes until a certain O-ring was changed out. So, I did just that. I red Xed my plane and signed off on the log. The part was on back order and I had no idea when it would come in. Enter my first sergeant. I was coming back from having the plane washed (which was kinda cool, I got to sit in the cockpit as the aircraft was towed to the washing area) and he asked me why the plane has been grounded for so long. I explained about the TO, and he told me to never mind, unground the plane and get it prepped for sorties (flights). I was a bit stunned, and mentioned that it was a TO and, as far as I knew, that meant that under no circumstances should the plane be allowed to fly until the part was changed. I got a lecture about how many stripes he had, how long he was in service, and how no one stripe should back talk to him and get the f-ing plane flying. I held my ground. After all, my name would be on the log and if anything went wrong, I doubted the sergeant would back me up. I refused and asked to see the squadron commander to sort out the issue. He backed down, but I knew I was done for. Long story short, he made my life miserable. Riding my ass constantly. One notable encounter of many: One time, I broke a sliding glass window, went to the dorm manager (guy in charge of our barracks) and told him I broke it. I apologized and offered to pay for it. He said not to worry, it had been getting stuck and breaking for years and I wasn’t the first person to do it. I thought the issue was resolved. The first sergeant called a dorm meeting, giving everyone crap about various things, and then he asks the group, “Ok who broke the window in the 2nd floor rec room?” I raised my hand. He looked at me and said, “I want the truth..who broke the window?” Perplexed, I stated, “I did..I’m sorry, I reported it.” This went on a few minutes, and he called me a liar. It turns out that he thought some other guy who was getting discharged broke it and had me say I did so he wouldn’t get into trouble. It doesn’t really make sense, as the dorm manager stated it wasn’t a big deal. When it went really bad: After a year of this, my mother got cancer and got a terminal diagnosis. After talking with several of my fellow airmen, they suggested that since all of the pressure I was getting was pretty rough, I ask for a hardship discharge to care for my mother. Honestly, I did not need the discharge, I have several siblings who were taking care of my mom, but I talked the situation up to get out before I got into real trouble. Just before my discharge, papers came through and the first sergeant called me to his office. He gave me a list of things that he claimed I broke (like the pool table, some doors, furniture, etc.) and said that before I could be released, I had to pay for all of it. I told him no way, I didn’t break any of that, and he told me, “Well, you can ask for a hearing on all of this, but it will take some time and you need to get home quick, don’t you?” I held myself together as I left his office, but when I got to work, I broke down and told my squadron commander what happened. He took me over to the base commander and intervened. He said as far as he knew, I wasn’t responsible for any of this, how the first sergeant was always unfair to me, etc. I really owe this guy because even though he was an officer, a first sergeant has a lot of pull and could have caused him grief. The end result: Well, after meeting with the base commander and the first sergeant to sign my discharge papers, the first sergeant handed me a paper. It was a form that said I was not eligible to ever re-join the USAF again. He said that if I signed that, everything else would be dropped and I’d be free to go with a hardship discharge under honorable conditions. I asked if he had a pen. So, there it is. I’m banned form re-joining the United States Air Force again. It was a shame, as I really enjoyed it at the start. NOTE: The US Army was hounding me shortly after to join them and train on helicopters. They did not give a crap about the US Air Force ban. I declined, but it was nice to be asked.

I was new to driving stick shifts and my truck stalled at the light and I could not for the life of my truck started when it changed to green. A cop started yelling at me to move on and was getting upset that I was blocking the street. As my face was turning beet-red from embarrassment, I cried out “I can’t, I’m stalled, sorry I’m trying”. He walked over to my window, leaned looking at me and my friend and said “Hold in a minute” he yelled to his partner to come over and help push my truck so I could pop the clutch. I kid you not his partner came over eating a donut (could have been a bagel, it was NYC) and stuck it in his mouth and they both pushed my truck down the street so I could start it. I got the truck going and with a wave the two cops left me to go on my way.

Question: Who would win in a fight between Batman and Spider-Man? Why?
Answer: There have been some great and well thought out answers here. My answer would be to quote the great Stan Lee "So one Question I'm always asked. Who would win in a fight? Who would win in a fight if Galactus fought The Hulk, or if Thor fought Iron Man? And there's one answer to all of that. It's so simple, anyone should know this. The person who'd win in a fight is the person that the scriptwriter wants to win! If I'm writing a story, about The Thing, from the Fantastic Four, and he gets into a big fight with Spider-Man, and millions of people out there say Who Would Win? Well, it depends on who I want to win if I'm writing the script. If I want Spider-Man to win, he'll win. If I want the Thing to win, he'll win. These are fictitious characters, the writer can do whatever he wants with them! So stop asking those questions, 'cause I've had it with that."
